user.title: Singapore
user.description:
Set up the Singapore integration.

Tariffs, COE, weather, train status and public holidays need no account. Tick the box below to also track your own SP Services electricity and water usage — that needs a one-time sign-in through your browser.

sp_login.title: Link SP Services account
sp_login.description:
SP Services enforces a captcha and an SMS OTP, so the sign-in happens in your browser and you hand the result back here.

1. Open this link and sign in to SP Services: {authorize_url}
2. Complete the captcha and the SMS OTP in the browser.
3. The browser then lands on `services.spservices.sg/callback?...` — copy that **full** URL. It often redirects away immediately; if you miss it, open developer tools (F12) → **Network**, tick **Preserve log**, sign in again, and copy the Request URL of the `callback` request.
4. Paste it below. It must contain both `code=` and `state=`, and it has to come from the link above — a callback from an earlier attempt is rejected.

If SP does not issue a refresh token for your account, the next step offers a way to keep the session alive.

sp_account.title: Choose SP Services account
sp_account.description: Several utility accounts are linked to this SP Services login. Pick the premises to track — one set of usage sensors is created for it.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-link SP Services account
reauth_confirm.description:
The SP Services session has ended and needs a fresh browser sign-in.

1. Open this link and sign in to SP Services: {authorize_url}
2. Complete the captcha and the SMS OTP in the browser.
3. The browser then lands on `services.spservices.sg/callback?...` — copy that **full** URL. It often redirects away immediately; if you miss it, open developer tools (F12) → **Network**, tick **Preserve log**, sign in again, and copy the Request URL of the `callback` request.
4. Paste it below. It must contain both `code=` and `state=`, and it has to come from the link above — a callback from an earlier attempt is rejected.

Your previously selected SP account is kept if it is still linked.

sp_session.title: Keep the SP Services session alive
sp_session.description:
SP issued no refresh token for this account, so the sign-in expires on its own — often within hours. Home Assistant can renew it unattended the same way the SP web portal does, using your Auth0 session cookie.

1. In the same browser you just signed in with, open developer tools (F12) → **Application** (Chrome/Edge) or **Storage** (Firefox) → **Cookies** → `https://identity.spdigital.auth0.com`.
2. Copy the **Value** of the cookie named `auth0`. It is HttpOnly, so it will not appear in `document.cookie` — devtools is the only way to read it.
3. Paste it below (the value alone is enough).

Home Assistant stores the cookie with your tokens and replaces it each time it renews, so the link lasts until SP ends the session itself — typically weeks — and only then are you asked to sign in again.

Leaving the field empty continues without a cookie (and clears one that was stored before). Usage sensors still work; you will just be asked to sign in again each time the access token expires. You can add the cookie later from **Configure** on the integration entry.

error.name_too_long: Name must be 64 characters or fewer.
error.invalid_callback: That callback URL did not contain a valid authorization code for this sign-in. Each attempt gets a new link, so use the one below and copy the callback URL it produces — including `code=` and `state=`.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach SP Services. Try again in a moment.
error.no_accounts: This SP Services login has no linked utility accounts.
error.invalid_session_cookie: SP would not renew a session with that cookie. Copy the `auth0` cookie value again from the browser you signed in with (it may have been rotated since), or leave the field empty to continue without it.

abort.reauth_successful: The SP Services account was re-linked.
